- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- phase-implementer: Implements one work package of a PLAN.md phase inside an isolated worktree. Spawned only by the /phase orchestrator with a self-contained delegation prompt. Not for ad-hoc edits. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Edit, Write)

- phase-verifier: Read-only auditor that verifies a phase's Definition of Done against actual repository state, item by item, with evidence. Spawned by /phase after tests pass, and by /handoff to validate handoff claims. Cannot modify anything. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- test-runner: Runs the full test suite (and smoke tests when asked) in an isolated context and returns only exact counts and failure details. Use whenever the full suite must run — /phase gate, /handoff evidence, or any "run the tests" request — so verbose output never floods the main conversation. (Tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob)

- handoff: Generate a validated end-of-session handoff for the next phase. Use at the end of every /phase run, when the user says /handoff, "wrap up the session", or "prepare handoff". Every claim in the handoff must be verified by the phase-verifier agent against actual repo state before it is written.
- phase: Execute one numbered phase end-to-end against its Definition of Done by orchestrating a fleet of parallel subagents. Use whenever the user says /phase, "run the next phase", "execute phase N", or wants a PLAN.md phase implemented. The main session orchestrates only — implementation is delegated to phase-implementer agents, testing to test-runner, and DoD verification to phase-verifier.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

# Amendment 2026-09-04 — Layer 1: Local Stats Engine (v0.7.0)

**Placement rule (measured):** `src/release/readme.test.ts` asserts that
`## Amendment 2026-08-26 — Version posture` is the **last** `## ` section of `agent-deck-spec.md`.
This amendment is therefore inserted **immediately before** that section, after the Codex
amendment, exactly as the OpenCode amendment was. It states no CC version number.

Forward-only and additive. Nothing above it changes. Design authority: `map.md` (project-internal,
in no repo), decisions L0, L1, L4, L6, L11. Baseline: **v0.6.0** as published 2026-09-04 — three
engines (`cc`, `opencode`, `codex`), display name "Agent Deck — Watch Your Agents Work.".
Release target: **v0.7.0**. Nothing here reaches the Marketplace until Phase 5 of the v0.7.0
`PLAN.md` closes and the user publishes.

---

## A. Problem statement

Agent Deck shows what a session is doing on three engines. It does not show what a session
**repeated**, **re-touched**, or **spent**. The same fixture corpus that pins three trees also
contains, structurally and without reading content: which files were touched how many times, which
tool calls recurred with identical input, which subagents did nothing, how the prompt moved turn over
turn, how full a context window is where the engine states one, and what an engine reports it cost.
Layer 1 exposes those **facts**. Interpretation is Layer 2, a separate closed product
(`agent-deck-insights`) that reaches these facts only through the API in §H.

## B. Non-goals

- No sentence of advice in the UI, README, CHANGELOG or model. A forbidden-word test enforces it.
- No content reading. A fact that needs the *text* of a tool input, result, or message is not a
  Layer 1 fact. "Was this shell call a test run?" is content; it is out.
- **No shipped price table.** `costUsd: 0` still means *not computed*; the repo holds no prices and a
  model-to-price map would be memory, which G6 forbids. Cost is shown only where an engine writes it
  **or where the user has entered prices for that model** (`agentDeck.pricing`, empty by default).
  A subscription plan is flat-rate and yields no per-token number, so no "provider" menu exists.
- No model-to-context-window lookup. Fill ratio exists only where the engine states `windowTokens`.
- No network, no exporter, no license, no second VSIX. Layer 1 lives in the public extension.
- No change to what the live deck renders. The stats surface is additive.

## C. Constraint amendments (Grounding Contract deltas)

Only these change. Each is copied into the v0.7.0 `PLAN.md` §Grounding Contract. Amending G-letters
is reserved to the user (CLAUDE.md reserved item 4); this section is that decision, recorded.

- **G1 — unchanged in scope, restated for three engines.** Never writes under `~/.claude`, the
  OpenCode data or config directories, or `~/.codex` / `$CODEX_HOME`. The only writable location
  Layer 1 adds is VS Code `globalStorage` (G7 below).
- **G2 — Source separation, extended.** The stats deriver is a **third consumer** downstream of every
  engine's grafter. It never feeds liveness or content. A deriver failure increments a diagnostics
  counter (`statsErrors`, on the existing channel) and is skipped; the deck renders identically with
  the deriver present, absent, or throwing.
- **G3 — Refuse, don't guess, extended.** Stats derive only for sessions with `schemaOk: true` and an
  empty `parked` list. Any other session is `excluded:<code>` with empty tables and is absent from
  every aggregate. No partial stats.
- **G4 — Redaction, extended.** `StatsRecord` string fields are an allow-list (`sessionId`, `agentId`,
  `toolName`, `filePath`, `engine`, enum codes, schema version). A corpus test asserts no thinking or
  reasoning text, no tool payload, no message text from any fixture appears in any record or store
  file — against **literal captured bytes**, the OpenCode/Codex G4 pattern, so it cannot be vacuous.
- **G6 — Fixtures are law, extended.** One committed golden `StatsRecord` per committed session
  fixture, all three engines. Engine change → regenerate by script → diff reviewed in the handoff.
- **G7 — Live-only, in-memory, AMENDED.** New text: *No persistence under any engine's directory;

# Execute a phase (orchestrator protocol)

You are the ORCHESTRATOR. You do not write implementation code yourself in this
mode. You decompose, dispatch, monitor, verify, and merge. Workers do the work.

## Phase 0 — Load, read, gate
1. Read PLAN.md. Identify the target phase number (from the user's argument, or
   the first phase not marked complete).
2. **Kickoff reading.** If the phase section declares a `**Kickoff reading**` list,
   read every entry in the listed order before extracting anything else. The list is
   the phase's own declaration of what its executor must understand — skipping an
   entry is a process failure, recorded as a deviation in the handoff. A phase
   section without the list gets the default: this file's Grounding Contract +
   Swarm Protocol, the phase section, and the current HANDOVER.md.
3. **Re-measure, do not read.** The plan's "Status as of planning" block — and
   HANDOVER/CLAUDE state claims generally — are snapshots that can be stale: this
   repo has closed phases, changed visibility, and rewritten history between
   planning and dispatch. Before presenting open questions, run the phase's
   declared re-measurement commands (default: `git log --oneline -5`,
   `git status --short`, `node scripts/privacy-sweep.mjs`) and compare them with
   the documents. If measurement disagrees with a document, the measurement wins
   and the discrepancy is raised at the gate — it is NOT patched into the
   documents mid-phase; the handoff fixes documents.
4. Extract: the phase's Definition of Done (DoD), module list, test
   expectations, and open-question checklist.
5. Present ALL open questions as ONE consolidated checklist, including any
   discrepancy found in step 3 as its own question. STOP and wait for answers.
   Do not dispatch anything until every question is resolved.

## Phase 1 — Decompose into work packages
6. Split the phase into work packages **partitioned by module boundary**.
   Hard rule: no two packages may own the same file. If two modules must touch
   the same file, merge them into one package.
7. For each package record: package ID, owned files/directories, the spec slice
   from PLAN.md relevant to it, the DoD items it satisfies, and its module-level
   test command.
8. Parallelization rules:
   - Packages with no dependency between them → dispatch in parallel.
   - Dependent packages → dispatch in dependency order (parallel within each wave).
   - A package touching fewer than ~3 files is not worth a worker — batch it
     with a neighbor or do it in the final integration step.
   - Cap concurrent implementers at 4 unless the user raises it.
9. Show the user the dispatch plan as a compact table (package → files → DoD
   items → wave). Proceed unless they object.

## Phase 2 — Dispatch the fleet
10. For each package in the current wave, spawn a `phase-implementer` subagent
    in the background. The delegation prompt MUST be self-contained — the worker
    sees nothing of this conversation. Include verbatim:
    - The package's spec slice from PLAN.md
    - The exact list of files it owns (and that it must touch nothing else)
    - The DoD items it is responsible for
    - The module test command it must pass before reporting
    - The required report format (defined in the agent file)
    - The budget law: write all the code first, run its module tests once, fix,
      run again; never run the full suite from a worker
11. While workers run, you may answer user questions but make no code edits.
    Track worker status; the user can watch /tasks.

## Phase 3 — Collect, merge, integrate
12. As each worker reports, check the report against the required format.
    A report missing evidence (test output, file list) is rejected: resume that
    SAME worker via SendMessage with what's missing — do not spawn a fresh one.
13. Workers run in isolated git worktrees. After a wave completes, merge each
    worktree branch into the phase branch. On merge conflict: the package
    partitioning failed — resolve manually in the main session and note the
    boundary violation for /handoff.
14. Perform any small glue/integration edits yourself (imports, wiring,
    config) — this is the only code the orchestrator writes.

## Phase 4 — Verify
15. Spawn `test-runner` to execute the FULL test suite. Do not proceed until it
    reports 100% pass with exact counts. On failures: resume the implementer
    that owns the failing module with the failure output. Repeat until green.
16. Spawn `phase-verifier` with the full DoD checklist. It returns PASS/FAIL
    per item with repo evidence. Any FAIL → route back to the owning
    implementer (resume, don't respawn), then re-verify. Do not self-certify;
    only the verifier's PASS counts.

## Phase 5 — Close
17. Commit on the phase branch with a clear message listing the DoD items
    satisfied and the exact test counts from test-runner's report.
18. Run /handoff. The handoff must supersede stale state documents: HANDOVER.md
    is rewritten for the next phase, and CLAUDE.md's "Current state" is brought
    to the closed phase — a closed phase whose state blocks still open on an
    earlier phase is this repo's most-repeated defect (PLAN's Phase 6 section
    records it against itself), and the verifier is to check for it.

## Failure and escalation rules
- A worker blocked on a spec ambiguity must report BLOCKED, not guess. Surface
  the question to the user, get an answer, resume the worker with it.
- If a worker exceeds its scope (edits an unowned file), discard its worktree,
  respawn with a tightened prompt.
- If the same package fails verification twice after resume, stop the fleet and
  escalate to the user with the verifier's evidence.
- Serial fallback: if the phase is tightly coupled (single module, shared
  state), skip the fleet and implement directly in the main session, then still
  run Phases 4–5 (test-runner + verifier are mandatory regardless).

## A. Problem statement

Agent Deck shows what a session is doing on three engines. It does not show what a session
**repeated**, **re-touched**, or **spent**. The same fixture corpus that pins three trees also
contains, structurally and without reading content: which files were touched how many times, which
tool calls recurred with identical input, which subagents did nothing, how the prompt moved turn over
turn, how full a context window is where the engine states one, and what an engine reports it cost.
Layer 1 exposes those **facts**. Interpretation is Layer 2, a separate closed product
(`agent-deck-insights`) that reaches these facts only through the API in §H.

## B. Non-goals

- No sentence of advice in the UI, README, CHANGELOG or model. A forbidden-word test enforces it.
- No content reading. A fact that needs the *text* of a tool input, result, or message is not a
  Layer 1 fact. "Was this shell call a test run?" is content; it is out.
- **No shipped price table.** `costUsd: 0` still means *not computed*; the repo holds no prices and a
  model-to-price map would be memory, which G6 forbids. Cost is shown only where an engine writes it
  **or where the user has entered prices for that model** (`agentDeck.pricing`, empty by default).
  A subscription plan is flat-rate and yields no per-token number, so no "provider" menu exists.
- No model-to-context-window lookup. Fill ratio exists only where the engine states `windowTokens`.
- No network, no exporter, no license, no second VSIX. Layer 1 lives in the public extension.
- No change to what the live deck renders. The stats surface is additive.

## C. Constraint amendments (Grounding Contract deltas)

Only these change. Each is copied into the v0.7.0 `PLAN.md` §Grounding Contract. Amending G-letters
is reserved to the user (CLAUDE.md reserved item 4); this section is that decision, recorded.

- **G1 — unchanged in scope, restated for three engines.** Never writes under `~/.claude`, the
  OpenCode data or config directories, or `~/.codex` / `$CODEX_HOME`. The only writable location
  Layer 1 adds is VS Code `globalStorage` (G7 below).
- **G2 — Source separation, extended.** The stats deriver is a **third consumer** downstream of every
  engine's grafter. It never feeds liveness or content. A deriver failure increments a diagnostics
  counter (`statsErrors`, on the existing channel) and is skipped; the deck renders identically with
  the deriver present, absent, or throwing.
- **G3 — Refuse, don't guess, extended.** Stats derive only for sessions with `schemaOk: true` and an
  empty `parked` list. Any other session is `excluded:<code>` with empty tables and is absent from
  every aggregate. No partial stats.
- **G4 — Redaction, extended.** `StatsRecord` string fields are an allow-list (`sessionId`, `agentId`,
  `toolName`, `filePath`, `engine`, enum codes, schema version). A corpus test asserts no thinking or
  reasoning text, no tool payload, no message text from any fixture appears in any record or store
  file — against **literal captured bytes**, the OpenCode/Codex G4 pattern, so it cannot be vacuous.
- **G6 — Fixtures are law, extended.** One committed golden `StatsRecord` per committed session
  fixture, all three engines. Engine change → regenerate by script → diff reviewed in the handoff.

  setting-disableable history of derived `StatsRecord`s under `context.globalStorageUri`. The store is
  never read back into `SessionState`; it feeds the Trends view and the API only.* The

- **G8, G9 — unchanged.** Golden stats derive from this repo's own harvested and redacted corpora.
- **New G10 — Facts only.** `src/stats/**`, `webview/stats/**`, and the `0.7.0` CHANGELOG block
  contain no interpretive language. Constants (`LOOP_MIN`, `SPIKE_TOKENS`) are named measurement
  parameters, displayed as such, not judgments.

1. **Files** — sorted by total touches; read/edit/write/error per row; rows flagged when in a loop or

2. **Loops & churn** — list; expanding shows the ordinals in the chain, each a link that fires the
   existing `select` intent on that tool node.
3. **Tokens** — per agent: prompt, output, cache ratio where available, context fill where available

4. **Trends** — from the store: prompt per session, loops per session, engine-reported cost per session
   where present, one point per session in order. Empty state when the store is disabled or holds
   fewer than two records.

Engine chips filter the stats view exactly as they filter the deck. Excluded sessions appear as a
footer count with reason codes, never in tables.

## I. Acceptance criteria (spec-level)

- Every committed session fixture, all three engines → byte-identical golden `StatsRecord`.
- Any parked or refused session → `excluded:<code>`, empty tables, absent from aggregates.
- No substring (≥ 12 bytes) of any fixture's thinking/reasoning, payload, or message text appears in
  any record or store file.
- Deriver throws → deck renders identically; `statsErrors` increments on the diagnostics channel.
- `agentDeck.stats.enabled = false` → zero files under `globalStorage/stats/`.

/**
 * Agent Deck — domain model, extension/webview message contract, and the
 * parser-facing types.
 *
 * Types only. No I/O, no dependencies, no logic beyond runtime type guards.
 * Everything Agent Deck holds is in-memory and discarded on window close
 * (G7); nothing here describes persisted state.
 */

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// (a) Domain model — session tree held in the extension host
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Tokens, split the way the model API actually bills and the way a context
 * window actually fills.
 *
 * MEASURED, and the reason this type exists at all. Assistant `usage` objects
 * in the committed Claude Code corpora carry `input_tokens` of roughly **2**
 * while the prompt itself sits in `cache_creation_input_tokens` +
 * `cache_read_input_tokens`. A field named `in` that reads `input_tokens`
 * alone therefore reports single digits for a five-figure prompt, and that is
 * what `0.1.2` shipped. `src/model/tokens.test.ts` pins the arithmetic to a
 * real captured message by `message.id`.
 *
 * **The "~2" is true of the caching corpora and NOT of all captured data.**
 * A session against a local model with no prompt caching puts the whole prompt
 * in `input_tokens` and leaves both cache fields at 0. **The sum rule is right
 * either way** — that is the point of summing all three rather than switching
 * on whichever field looks populated.
 *
 * `prompt` is the sum of all three, each defaulting to 0 when absent or
 * non-finite.
 *
 * **There is no `window` field, and that is a measurement, not an omission.**
 * No captured transcript states a context limit anywhere, so Agent Deck states
 * no percentage. A model-name-to-window lookup table would be memory rather
 * than fixture, which G6 forbids outright. `contextNow` is an absolute number
 * or it is nothing.
 */
export interface TokenPair {
  /**
   * Everything sent to the model for this message:
   * `input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens`.
   */
  prompt: number;
  /** `output_tokens`. */
  output: number;
}

export interface SessionState {
  sessionId: string; // <sessionId>.jsonl basename
  projectSlug: string;
  workspaceMatch: boolean;
  liveness: 'live' | 'idle' | 'ended' | 'unsupported';
  schemaOk: boolean;
  root: AgentNode;
  /**
   * What is left after the token split: cost, and nothing else.
   *
   * **`inputTokens` and `outputTokens` were REMOVED from this field**, not
   * renamed. They were the whole-session sums of the per-agent `in`/`out`
   * pair, so they carried the same defect {@link TokenPair} describes,
   * multiplied by the number of agents. A field that keeps its name and
   * changes its meaning is worse than one that goes away: the removal breaks
   * every reader at compile time, which is the point.
   *
   * `costUsd` is unchanged, and **0 still means NOT YET COMPUTED**, never
   * "free" — there is no price table in this repository and inventing one
   * would put a fabricated number in front of the user.
   */
  totals: { costUsd: number };
  /**
   * How full the session's context is **right now**: the last assistant
   * message of the main transcript, by ordinal.
   *
   * The main transcript, not the deepest subagent: each subagent has its own
   * window, and "how much room is left in the conversation I am watching" is a
   * question about the session's own thread. Per-agent figures live on
   * {@link AgentNode.contextNow}.
   *
   * Not a sum. A context window is a level, not a total — summing successive
   * prompts answers "how much was spent", which is {@link SessionState.burn}.
   *
   * **OPTIONAL because an engine may not report it, and absent is not zero.**
   * The OpenCode engine leaves this unset: its per-step token data lives in
   * `step-finish` part rows that nothing reads yet. A renderer shows
   * `EM_DASH` for absent and a real figure for present; writing 0 here would
   * claim an empty context window, which is a wrong number rather than a
   * missing one. See `src/opencode/graft.ts`.
   */
  contextNow?: TokenPair;
  /**
   * Everything the session has spent: summed across distinct `message.id`
   * over every agent in the tree, parked agents contributing nothing.
   *
   * This is the additive figure, and it is the one that grows without bound.
   * It is deliberately NOT what a node or a cell shows — a user watching a
   * long session wants to know how close to the ceiling they are, and burn
   * cannot answer that.
   *
   * **OPTIONAL for the same reason as {@link SessionState.contextNow}**, and
   * unset by the OpenCode engine for a DIFFERENT one worth recording: that
   * engine's `session.tokens_input` IS a genuine session-cumulative total —
   * measured, 24 of 24 sessions equal to the sum of their `step-finish`
   * rows — but it counts only UNCACHED input. Across the anchor corpus
   * `cache.read` sums to 8,875,276 against `input`'s 1,227,047, so mapping it
   * onto `prompt` would under-report by roughly 7x. That is precisely the
   * defect {@link TokenPair} exists to remove, so it is left absent rather
   * than filled with a plausible wrong total.
   */
  burn?: TokenPair;
  /**
   * Phase 2 additive, and optional so every Phase 1 construction of this
   * interface stays valid. The spec'd fields above are untouched.
   *
   * `ToolNode` has no `children` field and that stays true, so a subagent
   * `AgentNode` does NOT nest inside the `ToolNode` that spawned it: the
   * grafter places it adjacent in the parent agent's `children`. The real
   * spawn relationship therefore exists only here. A renderer that wants to
   * draw a subagent under its spawning tool call reads these edges; without
   * them that relationship is not recoverable from `root` alone.
   */
  spawnEdges?: readonly SpawnEdge[];
  /**
   * Agents the grafter knows exist and deliberately did NOT attach to the
   * tree, each with the machine-readable code saying why.
   *
   * Phase 4.5 additive, and optional for the same reason `spawnEdges` is:
   * every earlier construction of this interface stays valid, and no field
   * above changes meaning.
   *
   * A parked agent is absent from `root` on purpose — G3 refuses rather than
   * guessing a parent — so without this field a parked agent reaches the
   * webview through no channel at all, and "refuse, don't guess" is a decision
   * the renderer cannot see. `root` cannot recover it: there is nothing in the
   * tree to recover it from.
   *
   * An empty list is the honest value for a session that parks nothing, and it
   * is also what a refused (`schemaOk: false`) session carries: a refusal
   * renders nothing, and a new field is not a hole to smuggle content through.
   */

  /**
   * Which observation engine produced this state.
   *
   * Phase 4 additive, and optional for the third time and the same reason
   * `spawnEdges` and `parked` were: every earlier construction of this
   * interface stays valid and no field above changes meaning. **Absence reads
   * as `'cc'`**, which is what every state produced before the OpenCode engine
   * existed was. `agent-deck-spec.md` OC7 is the authority for the shape.
   *
   * The tag exists so ISOLATION is assertable: G2 gained a cross-engine half —
   * a corrupt or absent OpenCode database must leave CC sessions rendering
   * unchanged, and a CC parse failure must leave OpenCode sessions rendering
   * unchanged — and a test can only name the sessions that must be unaffected
   * if the state says which engine produced them.
   *
   * **Both of the scope lines Phase 4 wrote here have been crossed, by user
   * decision at the Phase 5 gate.** The paragraph that stood here said

   * `src/model/session.ts` produces a state carrying it. Neither is true from
   * Phase 5 on, and the old text is superseded rather than quietly corrected,
   * because a reader who trusts it will draw the wrong conclusion twice:
   *
   * - **`SessionFieldPatch` carries it** (gate amendment B2), for the
   *   uniformity DoD 5.1 asks for. The reasoning that argued against it still
   *   holds — the engine cannot change mid-session — so the key is one the
   *   model never emits. `SessionFieldPatch.engine` says so at its own site.
   * - **The CC engine STAMPS `'cc'`** (gate amendment B3). `session.ts` sets
   *   the field explicitly, so every state on the wire names its engine rather
   *   than leaving the CC case to be inferred from absence.
   *
   * The field stays OPTIONAL, and absence still reads as `'cc'`. Making it
   * required would invalidate every earlier construction of this interface,
   * which is the entire reason it — like `spawnEdges` and `parked` — was added
   * optional in the first place.
   */
  /**
   * **Widened for the Codex engine (v0.6.0 Phase 2, spec C11).** The field
   * keeps every property described above: still optional, absence still
   * reads as `'cc'`, and no earlier construction of this interface is
   * invalidated. Codex sessions are tagged `'codex'`.
   *
   * `src/bridge/diagnostics.ts` declares the same three-way union
   * SEPARATELY, because that module imports nothing at all by design. The
   * two declarations are kept in step by hand; `typecheck` is what catches
   * them drifting, and it did — widening only this one produced three
   * errors, which is how the second site was found rather than assumed.
   * Nothing emits a `'codex'` diagnostic until the host mounts the engine
   * in Phase 3 (DoD 3.2); the channel can carry one now so the pair does
   * not have to be widened twice.
   */
  engine?: 'cc' | 'opencode' | 'codex';

  /**
   * The model's context window for this session, in tokens — the third
   * number a Codex cell carries beside Context and Burn (Phase 0 decision
   * **D0.2**, spec C8).
   *

   * content of that case is that no child session id exists — OpenCode parks a

   * offers for the thing that was parked. `fixtures/opencode-1.18.22/GOLDEN.md`

export interface AgentNode {

########## fixtures/README.md
# Fixtures

**These are real Claude Code session transcripts, captured raw.** Parser and stitcher behavior is
pinned to them (grounding contract G6): a new CC version means capturing new fixtures *before*
changing code.

**As of Phase 3 they are no longer only Claude Code.** `opencode-1.18.22/` and `opencode-1.18.21/`
are real OpenCode SQLite stores, captured read-only from the same machine. G6 applies to them
identically — a new OpenCode data version means capturing before changing code — and so does the
raw-and-unredacted posture described under **Privacy** below.

## Contents

```
cc-2.1.234/projects/c--Users-dev-projects-agent-deck/
  05c5482d-….jsonl                     main transcript (Phase 1 harvest)
  05c5482d-…/subagents/agent-*.jsonl   4 subagent transcripts, one at spawnDepth 2
  05c5482d-…/subagents/agent-*.meta.json
  05c5482d-…/tool-results/b6uvpgxa4.txt  63,774-byte offloaded tool payload
  4299490e-….jsonl                     main transcript
  4299490e-…/subagents/agent-*.jsonl   1 subagent transcript
  4299490e-…/subagents/agent-*.meta.json
cc-2.1.246/                            THE PROVENANCE ANCHOR (2026-08-26). See its own README.
  head-5.jsonl                         first 5 lines of the main transcript, for the version path
  projects/c--…-agent-deck/
    07e6c820-….jsonl                   main transcript, R1 mirror pair, 16 lines
    07e6c820-…/subagents/agent-a676c705dca135e9d.jsonl   agent B, 6 scripted tool calls, 17 lines
    07e6c820-…/subagents/agent-a676c705dca135e9d.meta.json
cc-2.1.241/                            a session on a LOCAL local-model model. See its own README.
  projects/c--…-agent-deck/
    6082be25-….jsonl                   121 lines, no subagents, `atis` / `atis-latch` present
    6082be25-…/auto-mode-classifier-error.txt   an unrecognised file inside the session directory
cc-2.1.237/                            one content-destroyed transcript + its redaction script
synthetic-dropped-actions/             THE LIVENESS-DEFECT CORPUS (2026-08-27). See its own README.
  projects/c--…-agent-deck/
    41194183-….jsonl                   main transcript, 658 lines, 121 tool_use, CC 2.1.246
    41194183-…/subagents/               the TWO subagents the report concerns, both with sidecars
    41194183-…/tool-results/            two offloaded payloads, 54 KB and 327 KB
opencode-1.18.22/                      THE OPENCODE ANCHOR (2026-08-26). See its own README.
  opencode.db                          a real OpenCode SQLite store, built read-only from the
                                       live one's own DDL; the version is the DATA's
                                       session.version, never the binary's
opencode-1.18.21/                      the OpenCode drift WITNESS. See its own README.
  opencode.db                          the same project's older-version sessions, captured in
                                       the same read-only pass
codex-0.151.0-alpha.7.2/               THE CODEX ANCHOR (2026-09-02/03). See its own README.
  README.md                            GENERATED by scripts/capture-codex.mjs — the per-run
                                       thread/agent_path/nickname/depth tables live there
  <run>/home/.codex/sessions/…/*.jsonl rollout transcripts, one directory tree per run
  <run>/hook-stream.jsonl              that run's hook records, FILTERED at this boundary
  baseline/ dup-names/ long-output/    five runs; see the section below for what each proves
  resume-twice-v1/ spawn-shapes/
phase0-evidence/
  latency-*.log                        measured append→render latency samples
  synthetic-hook-events.jsonl          7 synthetic hook payloads (P0-2 evidence)
  hook-mechanism-timing.txt            node -e vs curl.exe cost with the listener down
PHASE0-VERDICT.md                      the Phase 0 gate decision, with evidence
SCRUB-EVIDENCE.md                      the Phase 1 history scrub, with verification output

hook-events/
  cc-2.1.234-redacted.jsonl            285 real hook payloads, content destroyed, key
                                       presence/absence preserved exactly (Phase 2)
  cc-2.1.234-sessionstart.jsonl        2 SessionStart events — the R3 onset proof, captured
                                       with the listener bound BEFORE a fresh session opened
  redact-capture.mjs                   derives both from a gitignored raw capture (--only filters)
golden/graft/                          2 grafted-tree goldens + regeneration README
golden/session/                        2 SessionState goldens + regeneration README

synthetic-layout/                      22 hand-mutated trees the fingerprint must refuse,
                                       incl. two carrying a <slug>/memory/ directory
synthetic-lines/                       8 malformed / drift line cases for the parser
synthetic-graft/                       7 join cases: unresolved, ambiguous, depth mismatch
```

### The OpenCode pair — an anchor and a witness

[`opencode-1.18.22/`](opencode-1.18.22/README.md) is the **anchor**: the version whose structure the
OpenCode fingerprint's required-table and required-column assertions are proved against.
[`opencode-1.18.21/`](opencode-1.18.21/README.md) is the **witness**, and it exists because it
disagrees with the anchor. What it witnesses is the `compaction` part shape: the anchor's compaction
part carries `tail_start_id`, the witness's do not, so **the pair is what proves that field
optional**. One corpus could not — a single version cannot tell an optional field from a required
one, and a fingerprint that required `tail_start_id` because the only capture happened to have it
would refuse every older session. Each corpus's own README carries its counts, its per-check table
and the verbatim compaction rows; they are generated by `scripts/capture-opencode.mjs` and are not
restated here, because a duplicated count goes stale on the next harvest.

Both directory names are the **data's** `session.version`, not the binary's. OpenCode self-updated
`1.18.22` → `1.18.23` underneath a Phase 2 measurement while the database held sessions of two
different data versions, so the binary's version number is not a property of the bytes it wrote.

Everything under `synthetic-*` is **hand-made, not captured**. Each tree says so in its slug
directory name (`SYNTHETIC-hand-mutated-not-captured`) and each corpus has its own README with a
per-case expectation table. Never treat them as evidence about CC's real behavior (G6).

The Phase 1 history scrub (see `SCRUB-EVIDENCE.md`) removed the Phase 0 orchestrator session and
`real-hook-events.jsonl` for carrying foreign-project content. The `05c5482d-…` session replaces
that coverage and was **manufactured, not found**: a fresh CC window in this workspace ran a scripted
burst that spawned three subagents in parallel, one of which spawned a child of its own, and one of
which produced an output large enough to force CC to offload it. That is why the set now has a
`spawnDepth: 2` agent carrying `parentAgentId`, and a `tool-results/` directory.

Privacy-checked before commit: zero hits for any foreign project name, the only `projects-*` token
present is `agent-deck`, and every `cwd` in every entry is this repo (G8).

**What it still does not cover:** a malformed line, a corrupt `.meta.json`, a missing join key, a
mutated layout, or a mid-file CC version change. The first four are supplied by the `synthetic-*`
corpus (G6 requires those be clearly labelled and never confused with captured data). The fifth is
covered as of Phase 4: versions are accepted within a window (patch ±5, minor ±1 off the anchor), so
mid-file drift is a `SchemaMismatch` only when it leaves that window. In-window drift is accepted.

# `cc-2.1.260` — the COMPACTION corpus

Captured 2026-09-05 for v0.7.0 Phase 0, DoD 0.3b. Real Claude Code session, captured raw and then
redacted; G6 applies to it exactly as it applies to every other corpus here.

**Why it exists.** No committed corpus held a structural compaction entry, so fact **F12**
(compaction events: count, ordinal, turns since session start, prompt tokens either side) rested on
nothing. This session holds **two** compactions of **different triggers**, which is what makes it
able to answer the question rather than merely exhibit one.

**It also closes two gaps nobody harvested it for**, and both are worth more than they cost:

- **The only real `Edit` calls in any committed corpus.** Before this, `Edit` appeared **only** in
  `fixtures/synthetic-dropped-actions/` (32 calls, hand-made). Fact **F4** — the churn chain — is
  defined on `Edit/Write`, so its entire evidence base was synthetic. This corpus carries **18 real
  `Edit` calls** beside 32 `Write` and 39 `Read`.
- **A real mid-file CC version change.** The session's lines carry **two** versions (below). Every
  earlier mid-file-drift case in this repository is synthetic. This one is real and it is
  *in-window*, so it is a positive control for the version posture: it must be **accepted**.

## Provenance

| | |
|---|---|
| session | `75ef0bbf-2493-4c77-8af7-3a56fb2ce36e` |
| captured | 2026-09-05, from this machine's live `~/.claude/projects/` |
| lines | 2,028 parsed, **0 malformed** |
| versions on the lines | `2.1.258` ×1,225 and `2.1.260` ×201 |
| subagents | 3, each with its `.meta.json` sidecar |
| `tool-results/` | 1 offloaded payload |
| tool calls | `Bash` 218 · `Read` 39 · `Write` 32 · `Edit` 18 · `Skill` 3 · `Agent` 3 · `ToolSearch` 2 · `TaskStop` 1 |

**The directory is named `cc-2.1.260`, and the majority of its lines say `2.1.258`.** That is
deliberate and it is the honest name: **both compaction entries are written by `2.1.260`**, and the
compaction entries are the reason the corpus exists. Naming it for the majority version would name
it for the half that proves nothing. The version is read from the transcript's own `version` field,
never from the binary on `PATH` — the recorded rule, and this session is its own illustration, since
one binary wrote lines under two version strings.

## The two compaction entries

The structural entry is `type: "system"` carrying a `compactMetadata` object. Each is immediately
followed by a `type: "user"` entry with `isCompactSummary: true` — the summary CC injects in place
of what it dropped.

| line | type | `trigger` | `preTokens` | `postTokens` | `cumulativeDroppedTokens` |
|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **1933** | `system` | **`auto`** | 967,149 | 20,346 | 946,803 |
| 1934 | `user` | — (`isCompactSummary: true`) | | | |
| **2006** | `system` | **`manual`** (a `/compact`) | 276,178 | 24,938 | 1,198,043 |
| 2007 | `user` | — (`isCompactSummary: true`) | | | |

**Do their shapes match? YES — the key sets are identical**, measured rather than eyeballed. Both
`compactMetadata` objects carry exactly:

`cumulativeDroppedTokens`, `durationMs`, `postTokens`, `preCompactDiscoveredTools`, `preTokens`,
`preservedMessages`, `preservedSegment`, `trigger`

They differ only in **key order** within the object, which JSON does not carry meaning in, and in
their values. So per the locked Phase 0 answer: **a manual `/compact` is a valid F12 fixture
source** — one reader handles both, and `trigger` is what separates them, so F12 can record
`source: 'auto' | 'manual'` from the entry itself with nothing inferred.

**`preTokens` and `postTokens` are stated by the entry.** F12 wanted "prompt tokens on the turn
before and after **where the entries state them**"; here they are stated outright, so that half of
F12 needs no turn-walking at all.

## What was done to the bytes

Two redactors, in this order. Both are the existing route; neither is new for this corpus.

1. **`lab/tools/redact-paths.mjs`** (identity-token driven, 45 tokens, the private set) —
   `files=8 changed=4 renamed=0 exempt=0 **skipped=0**`, 905 replacements across ten token classes.
2. **`scripts/redact-paths.mjs`** (path shapes → `<HOME>`/`<USER>`/`<HOST>`) — `files=8 skipped=0
   changed=4`, 1,175 hits.

Before either, the repository path and the project slug were rewritten to the same scrubbed form
every other committed CC corpus already carries — slug `c--Users-dev-projects-agent-deck`, `cwd`
`C:\Users\dev\projects\agent-deck` — in all four spellings that occur (JSON-escaped, Windows,
forward-slash, MSYS). 2,671 replacements.

**The slug needs its own step because the redactor deliberately will not touch it**: the slug uses
`-` as its separator so no absolute-path pattern matches it, and it is a **join key**
(`projectSlug`; `src/opencode/slug.ts` pins the two engines' agreement on it). It is also identity
token #1, and the identity class has **no allow rule** — a hit fails the gate outright. Leaving it
alone was therefore not an option, and rewriting it by hand was.

**`node scripts/privacy-sweep.mjs --untracked` → `VERDICT PASS identity=0 secrets=0 foreign=0`.**
It read `FAIL identity=527` before the identity redactor ran, on the untracked working tree, which
is the order that matters: nothing was committed until it read zero.

**What redaction did NOT move**, verified after the fact: line count, parse result (2,028 / 0
malformed), both version strings and their counts, every tool-call name and count, all three
sidecars, the offloaded payload, and both `compactMetadata` objects including every token figure in
the table above.

## What this corpus does not prove

- **Nothing about compaction on any other engine.** OpenCode has its own `compaction` part shape
  (see the OpenCode pair's READMEs) and Codex's is unmeasured. F12 per engine is a Phase 0 question
  answered in `docs/evidence/phase-0-stats/VERDICT.md`, not here.
- **Nothing about a compaction that CC writes differently.** Two entries from one session on one
  version pair is a witness, not a census; a third trigger value, or a `compactMetadata` without
  `preTokens`, would be new information.
- **It is not the provenance anchor.** `src/parser/fingerprint.ts`'s `PINNED_CC_VERSION` is
  unchanged and still names `cc-2.1.246`. This corpus moves no anchor and no version window.

A real Claude Code session carrying TWO structural compaction entries of
different triggers, harvested so fact F12 rests on captured bytes rather than on
nothing. `fixtures/cc-2.1.260/README.md` is the record.

  line 1933  system  compactMetadata.trigger = "auto"    preTokens 967,149 -> post 20,346
  line 2006  system  compactMetadata.trigger = "manual"  preTokens 276,178 -> post  24,938

each followed by a `user` entry with `isCompactSummary: true`.

THEIR KEY SETS ARE IDENTICAL, measured rather than eyeballed - eight keys, the
same eight, differing only in order within the object and in their values. So
the locked open question resolves to its first branch: a manual `/compact` is a
valid F12 fixture source, one reader handles both, and `trigger` lets F12 record
`source: 'auto' | 'manual'` from the entry with nothing inferred. `preTokens` and
`postTokens` are stated outright, so the "tokens either side" half of F12 needs
no turn-walking.

TWO GAPS IT CLOSES THAT IT WAS NOT HARVESTED FOR.

- The only real `Edit` calls in any committed corpus. F4 (churn chain) is defined
  on `Edit/Write` and every `Edit` in this repository was previously hand-made,
  in `fixtures/synthetic-dropped-actions/`. G6 says synthetic is never evidence
  about real behaviour, so F4's evidence base was empty. This adds 18 real ones.
- A real mid-file CC version change: 1,225 lines say `2.1.258` and 201 say
  `2.1.260`. Every earlier drift case here is synthetic, and this one is
  in-window, so it is a positive control - it must be ACCEPTED.

The directory is named for `2.1.260` although most lines say `2.1.258`, because
both compaction entries are written by `2.1.260` and they are why the corpus
exists. The version is read from the transcript, never from the binary; this
session is its own illustration of why.

REDACTION, AND THE STEP THE ROUTE DOES NOT COVER. Both existing redactors ran
(`lab/tools/redact-paths.mjs`, 905 identity replacements, skipped=0; then
`scripts/redact-paths.mjs`, 1,175 path hits). Before them the repository path and
project slug were rewritten by hand, in all four spellings that occur, to the
scrubbed form every other CC corpus carries - 2,671 replacements.

That hand step is necessary because the redactor DELIBERATELY will not touch the
slug: it separates on `-`, so no absolute-path pattern matches it, and it is a
join key. It is also identity token #1, and the identity class has no allow rule
and no advisory tier - a hit fails the gate. So leaving it was not an option.

The sweep read FAIL identity=527 on the untracked tree before the identity
redactor ran, and PASS identity=0 after. Nothing was committed until it read
zero, which is the only order that helps: history is forever.

strings and counts, every tool name and count, all three subagent sidecars, the
offloaded payload, and both compactMetadata objects including every token figure
above. 6.38 MB raw, 1.66 MB packed.

## What this project is

Agent Deck is a **read-only** VS Code extension that renders live Claude Code session topology — subagent trees, in-flight tool calls, token/cost totals — by observing CC's exhaust. It never wraps, proxies, launches, or configures Claude Code.

Two independent data sources, deliberately:

- **Hooks → liveness.** A documented, stable Anthropic contract with poor payloads. User-installed hook snippet POSTs to a loopback HTTP listener. Answers "what is running right now."
- **JSONL → content.** `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl`, undocumented and drift-prone. Answers "what happened."

The split is the core architectural bet: schema drift degrades the UI instead of killing it. Never let content parsing and liveness share a failure path.

## Grounding contract (build-time law, all phases)

From `PLAN.md` — these gate review, not just style:

- **G1 Read-only, always.** No writes to CC settings, session files, or `~/.claude`, ever. Hook installation is a manual README paste block. Any code path writing outside the repo/extension storage fails review.
- **G2 Source separation.** A JSONL parse failure must never take down liveness rendering.
- **G3 Refuse, don't guess.** Schema fingerprint mismatch → session renders `unsupported`, never a partial tree. Malformed lines increment a counter and are skipped; never crash on input.
- **G4 Redaction is production code from Phase 1.** Thinking blocks dropped at the parse boundary; payloads truncated (8 KB default) with marker. The "no thinking content reaches the session model" test runs in every phase's suite.
- **G5 Zero egress.** No network except the loopback hook listener; non-loopback POSTs dropped.
- **G6 Fixtures are law.** Parser/stitcher behavior is pinned to fixtures captured from real sessions in Phase 0. New CC version → capture new fixtures *before* changing code.

## Architecture

```
JSONL append → tailer (byte offsets) → parser + fingerprint → redaction
                                                                  ↓
hook POST → loopback listener → liveness engine  →  session model (in-memory)
                                                    correlator · tree stitcher
                                                                  ↓ postMessage diffs
                                                          Svelte webview (pure renderer)
```

All state lives in the extension host and is in-memory only — no database, no persistence, discarded on window close. The webview receives snapshot/diff messages and sends back only UI intents (`expandNode`, `selectSession`); it has no fs or network access (CSP-enforced).

**Component 5 is not what the spec says it is.** Phase 0 disproved the interleaved-sidechain
premise on CC 2.1.234 — see `fixtures/PHASE0-VERDICT.md`, which supersedes the spec's Component 5
until the spec is amended. Measured: **0** `"isSidechain":true` entries in main transcripts and
**0** `Task` tool calls (the spawning tool is named `Agent`). Subagents get their own files:

```
projects/<slug>/<sessionId>.jsonl                                main transcript
projects/<slug>/<sessionId>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl      subagent transcript
projects/<slug>/<sessionId>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.meta.json  {agentType, description, toolUseId, spawnDepth, parentAgentId?}
projects/<slug>/<sessionId>/tool-results/<id>.txt                offloaded large tool payloads
```

`meta.toolUseId` names the exact parent `tool_use` block, so attribution is a **primary-key join**,
not an inference: 27/27 resolved, 0 ambiguous, across four sessions and three CC versions. The
stitcher is multi-file tailing plus a keyed graft; parents may themselves be agent transcripts
(`spawnDepth >= 2` verified on real data). The risk moved rather than vanished — everything now
rests on an undocumented directory convention, so Phase 1's fingerprint must assert the **layout**,
not just field names.

`agent-deck-spec.md` still carries the `SessionState` / `AgentNode` / `ToolNode` interfaces and the
message contract — those shapes survive unchanged and remain the source of truth.

  spike stitcher's internal convention. A correlator matching that string silently drops every
  main-thread event — absence of the key is the signal.
- **Hook payloads carry `agent_id` and `tool_use_id`**, the same join keys the JSONL layout uses, so
  liveness attaches to stitched nodes by join, not heuristic.
- **`SubagentStart` is CONFIRMED as of Phase 2** (2026-08-19), and every document that called it
  "never observed" was measuring our own configuration, not CC. It had never been *registered* in the
  hook block, so it could not have fired. It was registered at `74c5236` and arrived immediately —
  3/3 well-formed events, without a CC restart, so settings are re-read per hook invocation. Pinned
  in `fixtures/hook-events/cc-2.1.234-redacted.jsonl`. Two consequences: it carries **no
  `tool_use_id`** (0/3), so the hook tap alone cannot graft a subagent onto its spawning `tool_use`
  block — that join stays with the sidecar's `meta.toolUseId`; and `SubagentStop` carries
  **`agent_transcript_path`**, pointing exactly at `<sessionId>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl`, so
  the undocumented layout now has a second witness from the *documented* tap.
- **`SessionStart` is CONFIRMED on 2.1.234** (2 events, `fixtures/hook-events/cc-2.1.234-sessionstart.jsonl`).
  Its long absence was an artefact of listener bind order, never evidence about CC: it fires at
  session *onset*, so a listener that binds mid-session can never see it. Its payload is the
  **smallest** of any event — `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `hook_event_name`, `source`
  (`"startup"`) — with no `agent_id`, no `tool_use_id` and **no `prompt_id`**, which every other event
  carries. Liveness must still never *require* it.
- **Hook commands must fail fast when nothing is listening.** `curl.exe` burns its full connect
  timeout on a closed loopback port (~1.14 s, exit 28); `node -e` gets ECONNREFUSED and exits 0
  (~0.19 s). Never ship a paste block that stalls a user's real session.
- **`tool-results/*.txt` offloading exists.** Large tool payloads live *outside* the JSONL entirely.
  Redaction and truncation must cover that path or previews silently miss content.
- **The PATCH COMPONENT IS NOT COMPARED, and widening the box is not the fix. Changed 2026-08-26 in
  the `v0.1.2` hotfix; the dated "Amendment 2026-08-26 — Version posture" section of
  `agent-deck-spec.md` is the authority.** `fingerprint.ts` anchors on `PINNED_CC_VERSION` and
  accepts major exact, minor ±1, patch anything. **This is the second time the same defect shipped.**
  Phase 4 turned an exact pin into a box of patch ±5 after CC self-updated to `2.1.237` and 6 of 12
  of this repo's sessions went dark. That box topped out at `2.1.239`, CC shipped `2.1.240`, and from
  2026-08-24 **every session on every user's machine** rendered `unsupported` — with `v0.1.1` live on
  the Marketplace. A tolerance counted in patch releases is a countdown, not a policy. If you find
  yourself widening it a third time, the answer is that the string is the wrong signal.
  **`PINNED_CC_VERSION` is a PROVENANCE anchor, not a support claim** — it names the release whose
  captured fixture proved the structure (`fixtures/cc-2.1.246/`), moves only with a harvest, and
  moving it cannot make a version work because the patch number is not consulted.
  `src/parser/corpus.test.ts` asserts the anchor names a corpus that exists and carries it, so
  moving the constant without harvesting fails.
  **What refuses in range is the STRUCTURE**: `REQUIRED_ENTRY_FIELDS`, `REQUIRED_META_FIELDS` and the
  subagent layout. `fixtures/synthetic-structure-2.1.246/` is the proof — the anchor's own head slice
  with `uuid` renamed on line 3, carrying `2.1.246` exactly, still refused. A session file spanning
  versions is accepted while every version stays in range and refused as `versionChangedMidFile`
  otherwise. **What this buys and costs:** a release nobody captured is a release nobody verified, so
  structural drift surfaces as a wrong tree rather than a refusal — which is why the structural
  assertions were NOT loosened alongside the string.
- **A refusal fixture whose version quietly becomes acceptable does not fail. It passes, while
  testing nothing.** `synthetic-layout/07` and `08` have been re-versioned twice for exactly this:
  `2.1.235` → `2.1.400` (Phase 4's box accepted `2.1.235`) → `4.4.0` (dropping the patch comparison
  accepted `2.1.400`). `4.4.0` is out of range on the major **and** the minor component so no move of
  the anchor inside `2.x` can re-admit it. **Whenever `isVersionAccepted` moves, re-check those two
  and every hard-coded version in `fingerprint.test.ts`** — the 2026-08-26 change silently made
  `2.1.178`, `2.1.400` and a `pinnedVersion: '2.1.999'` override all *accepted*, and three tests were
  asserting refusals that would have stopped happening.
- **Project-slug drive-letter case varies** on Windows (`c--Users-…` and `C--Users-…` both occur).
  Match case-insensitively.
- **The `claude` on PATH cannot run at all, and the binary that writes the sessions lives inside the
  VS Code extension.** `claude --version` on PATH prints `Error: claude native binary not installed`
  (a stale npm global whose postinstall never completed). The real one is
  `~/.vscode/extensions/anthropic.claude-code-<version>-win32-x64/resources/native-binary/claude.exe`,
  which prints `2.1.246 (Claude Code)` as of 2026-08-26 and is what wrote `fixtures/cc-2.1.246/`.
  **Any fixture harvest must invoke that path**, or it captures nothing and reports a version from an
  install that is not observing anything. Also measured: `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` is
  refused by this environment's command classifier; a scripted harvest goes through explicit
  `--allowedTools` plus `--add-dir`, with a fixed `--session-id` so the harvest cannot pick up the
  wrong file.
- **Fixtures must stay replayable without `~/.claude`.** `CLAUDE_PROJECTS_ROOT` overrides the live
  projects root; the negative control (no env var, fake HOME) must fail ENOENT rather than silently
  falling back.
- **Hooks are installed in the repo-local `.claude/settings.local.json`**, not `~/.claude`. That is
  deliberate and keeps G1 absolute — nothing under `~/.claude` is ever written. That file is
  committed and its hook block is **live**: every tool call in this repo POSTs to `127.0.0.1:47821`.
  The POST is unconditional, but `spike/hook-events-real.jsonl` (gitignored) only grows while a
  listener is actually bound — with nothing listening the POST takes ECONNREFUSED and appends
  nothing. Do not read a stable line count as evidence that hooks stopped firing.
- **CC's thinking blocks are empty on disk; the `signature` carries the bytes.** All 15 thinking
  blocks in the committed capture have an **empty `thinking` string** and a long populated
  `signature`. A G4 test asserting only that thinking *text* does not leak is therefore vacuous — it
  would pass forever while proving nothing. Redaction drops the `signature` field too, and the G4
  test asserts against the literal captured signature bytes.
- **CC's size labels are KiB, not KB.** The `<persisted-output>` stub reports a 63,774-byte payload
  as "62.3KB". Do not convert its numbers as decimal KB.
- **The `.gitattributes` rule marking fixtures as non-text is load-bearing.** `core.autocrlf=true` is set on this
  machine and there was no `.gitattributes` until Phase 1. Without that rule a fresh clone checks the
  fixtures out with CRLF endings, shifting every byte offset in every transcript — which breaks
  byte-exact tests on every machine except the one that captured the data, and looks like a parser
  bug rather than a checkout artifact. Verify by cloning and comparing bytes, never by inspecting the
  working tree you already have.
- **`git config core.longpaths true` is required, and it is repo-local.** Worktree creation fails
  outright with `Filename too long` otherwise — the fixture paths run ~150 characters and, added to a
  temp-rooted worktree, exceed Windows MAX_PATH. The same bites `git clone`: cloning into a deep
  directory fails **at checkout**, so pass `git -c core.longpaths=true clone` and clone somewhere
  short. "Replay from a clean checkout" is a DoD criterion, so this is not cosmetic — the repo works
  today partly because its own path happens to be short.
- **Subagents read a stale snapshot of `CLAUDE.md` and `git status`.** What a spawned agent sees is
  the state at the *parent session's* start, not at spawn time. Two `test-runner` runs in Phase 1
  confidently reported "CLAUDE.md documents RESOLVED 6" long after the file said 5, because they were
  quoting the injected snapshot rather than reading the file. When an agent reports a file's
  contents, verify against the file — and put facts an agent must act on in its prompt, not in
  CLAUDE.md.
- **A tracked test file contains a real NUL byte** (`src/parser/parse.test.ts`, deliberate fuzz
  input). Any `git log -p --all | grep …` audit must pass `-a`, or GNU grep abandons the stream and
  returns a clean-looking, meaningless result. This silently defeats the privacy residual check.
- **Implementer worktrees are cut from `main`, not the current branch.** A worker dispatched during a
  phase starts without that phase's merged work unless it first runs
  `git merge --ff-only <phase-branch>`. Put that instruction in every delegation prompt.
- **A subagent spawn briefly presents a sidecar with no transcript, and the fingerprint refuses the
  whole session for it.** CC writes `agent-<id>.meta.json` **before** `agent-<id>.jsonl` — measured
  at **+0.080 to +0.120 s across 5 of 5 spawns** in one real session. In that window
  `fingerprintSession` returns `subagentTranscriptMissing` and the session renders `unsupported`,
  with no tree, until the next successful graft. Reproduced against real session data; the same data
  intact returns `ok: true`, so **the refusal depends on when you looked, not on what is there**.
  `DEFAULT_DEBOUNCE_MS = 120` is the same order as the gap, so it is likely rather than rare. Do not
  "fix" this by deleting the check — that check is the tripwire for the subagent directory convention
  moving. See `PLAN.md` **Found in the field / F1**, which carries the measurements and the candidate
  shapes.

- **`vitest` and `tsc` disagree about duplicate imports, and vitest is the one that lies.**
  `esbuild` silently tolerates the same specifier imported twice; `tsc --noEmit` reports
  `TS2300 Duplicate identifier` and exits 2. A file can therefore be 54/54 green while
  `npm run typecheck` is broken, which is exactly how a "typecheck 0" claim reached a commit
  message in this repo. **A green test file is not a typecheck.**

- **`esbuild-svelte` does not propagate Svelte compiler warnings.** Measured both ways: removing
  a `svelte-ignore` and adding an unused CSS selector each produced `warnings: []`. Combined with
  the fact that no type checker covers `.svelte` and eslint does not lint them, "the component
  build is green" says very little. Do not treat a clean build as a check on component code.

- **`element.click()` throws on SVG elements in jsdom.** `HTMLElement.prototype.click` is not on
  `SVGElement`, and every canvas cell, dot and blob is SVG. Dispatch a `MouseEvent`;
  `webview/testkit.ts` exports `press` for this.

- **`toSessionState` in `src/model/graft.ts` has NO production callers** and sets neither
  `spawnEdges` nor `parked`. The production path is `SessionModel.viewFromSnapshot`. This is not
  cosmetic dead code: a worker reached for the obvious-looking function, got behaviour production
  never produces, and an entire decision was taken on the wrong premise before it was measured.
  Same class as `DataPathOptions.graft`.

- **The webview stage transform is a TRANSFORM, never a coordinate.** Pan and zoom on both the
  deck and the session interior are an SVG transform on a wrapper group. `layout.ts` stays a pure
  function of state, its goldens stay valid as numbers, and "a spawn adds, it never reflows"
  survives a user dragging the view around. An implementation that edited placements instead
  would break all three **silently** — `webview/store.test.ts` pans, zooms, then asserts
  `deckLayout` output is byte-identical, which is the test that catches the wrong shape.

- **Separation must use a CONSTANT footprint, not the drawn radius.** `cellRadius` grows with a
  cell's child count, so separating on it means one new tool call changes a radius, changes a
  collision, and MOVES A CELL ALREADY ON SCREEN. Measured: the incremental golden test failed
  immediately with `cell a69e0f453d5ca5f43 y moved`. `CELL_FOOTPRINT` is therefore fixed at
  `LABEL_PAD + CELL_RADIUS_MAX`, and a guard test asserts the literal agrees with the constant it
  was derived from.

- **The wide thing on the canvas is the TEXT, not the circle.** An agent label is ~26 characters
  at 15px — several hundred units — on a membrane of radius ~35. Separating on the membrane
  produced circles with clear space between them and labels written straight through each other,
  which reads to a user as "nothing was fixed". Cells separate on `LABEL_PAD`, and
  `LABEL_MAX_CHARS` is the single constant both the padding and the truncation derive from.

- **A stray file at the repo root escapes a `docs/**`-shaped `.vscodeignore` rule and ships.** A
  duplicate of the 38 KB design mockup was committed at the root by a scripted edit and went into
  the VSIX; `docs/ui/**` did not match it there. **The only way this class shows up is unzipping
  the artifact and listing it** — `npx vsce ls` — because the ignore file alone cannot answer
  "what does the package actually contain". Same family as the manifest/build disagreement that
  produced the inert `.js` host bundle.

- **Backticks inside a shell-quoted `node -e` are command substitution.** Writing generated source
  through `node -e "...\`Store.enterSession\`..."` let bash eat every backticked identifier and
  silently produce prose with holes in it — "both deck components now take , the constellation
  renders". It does not error. Write generated text through a **script file**, never a
  shell-quoted one-liner; the same rule the NUL-byte trap already taught.

- **`git commit -m "…"` is a shell-quoted string, so backticks inside it are command substitution.**
  The recorded `node -e` trap, on the one command every session runs. A message containing
  ``lands in `ignored` `` and ``the `atis` key`` committed as "lands in ." and "the  key" — no error,
  no warning, and the damage is only visible in `git log`. **Write commit messages through a file and
  `git commit -F <file>`**, with the file written by the Write tool.
- **`String.replace` TREATS $' IN THE REPLACEMENT AS "EVERYTHING AFTER THE MATCH",
  and it will silently duplicate a whole file.** JavaScript's
  `String.prototype.replace(needle, replacement)` honours $&, $`, $' and $$ in the
  REPLACEMENT even when the needle is a plain string, not a RegExp. A patch script whose
  replacement text quoted the shell fragment `grep -c $'\r$'`
  therefore spliced the remainder of the file back in at that point: **`HANDOVER.md` tripled and
  `CLAUDE.md` doubled**, on 2026-08-29, with no error and no warning. The only symptom was a
  section heading appearing three times, and `wc -l` looking too big - neither of which any test
  in this repository checks. Both files were rebuilt from git and re-applied with **slice-based**
  replacement (`t.slice(0,i) + replacement + t.slice(i+len)`), which has no substitution syntax
  at all. **Use slice, never `.replace()`, for document edits**, and probe a patched document by
  counting one of its own headings. Fourth member of the quoting-metacharacter family this file
  records - after the backtick in a shell-quoted `node -e`, the backtick in `git commit -m`, and
  the quoted heredoc - and the first where the tool doing the mangling is not a shell at all.

- **A quoted heredoc through the Bash tool is not reliably literal.** `python - <<'PY'` with
  `\\b` and `\\s` on the same regex line delivered `\b` (one backslash, which Python then read as a
  backspace) and `\\s` (two) — measured, same line, same heredoc. A patch script that matches source
  containing regex literals will silently find nothing. Use the Write tool for the script, or the
  Edit tool for the change; this is the same lesson as the backtick trap and the NUL-byte trap, and
  it is now three for three.
- **Source files in this working tree are CRLF; `fixtures/` is LF.** Measured across 315 tracked
  files: 150 CRLF / 152 LF / 8 no-newline, but outside `fixtures/` (which `.gitattributes` keeps LF
  deliberately) it is 150 CRLF to 10 LF — `src/` 50:1, `webview/` 61:2, root 18:1. Any scripted patch
  that reads a source file preserving newlines and matches on `\n`-joined text finds nothing.
  Normalise, patch, restore the original ending.
- **`grep -c $'\r' <file>` RETURNS 0 ON A CRLF FILE, and it is the check most likely to be
  reached for when verifying a scripted edit did not eat the line endings.** GNU grep strips a
  trailing CR before matching end-of-line, so the pattern never matches. Measured 2026-08-30 on a
  file that had just been rewritten: `grep -c` said **0** and `tr -cd '\r' | wc -c` said **97**,
  against 97 lines. The file was perfect and the check said it had been destroyed — the opposite
  failure to the usual one, and it would have sent the next reader rebuilding a correct file.
  **Count with `tr -cd`, and compare the CR count to the LF count.** This is the same grep
  behaviour the corrected CI guard already records, arriving through the other door: there it
  made a broken check look clean, here it makes a clean file look broken.

- **A quoted heredoc mangles `\r\n` as well as `\\`, and the damage is silent and mixed.**
  `python - <<'PY'` writing generated source delivered `\n` where the script said `\r\n`, so an
  inserted block was LF inside a file that is CRLF throughout, and separately turned `.split('\\n')`
  into a real newline inside a string literal. The second one at least fails loudly — esbuild
  says `Unterminated string literal` and points at the line. **The first one does not fail at
  all**: it produces a file that compiles, passes, and breaks the next scripted patch that reads
  it. Third measured instance of this trap after the `\\b`/`\\s` case. **Write the script with the
  Write tool.** And after any scripted edit, assert `CR == LF` on the whole file, which catches
  the silent half.

- **Do not assert fixture-set *sizes* in tests.** Counts hard-coded against the capture break on the
  next harvest and read as regressions. Derive them from the directory, or assert behaviour.

- **Subagent nesting is capped at 2 by this repo's own settings.** The same committed file sets
  `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH: "2"` (and `MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS: "6"`). That is why
  depth-2 is the deepest real data on disk and why any depth-3 proof had to be synthetic — raise the
  cap before expecting deeper trees from live capture.

- **A commit that both changes a file and describes that file's state will describe the *old* state.**
  This is the single most repeated defect in this repo's history, and Phase 2 committed it three
  times: a test count written just before two merges moved it, a "closed PASS 9/9" written while the
  verdict on record was `FAIL 8/9`, and a risk bullet saying a file "says nothing about X" in the very
  commit that made it say X. **Diff the two halves of your own commit against each other before
  committing.** Never write a live number or a verdict into a document from inside the phase that
  changes it — write what was verified and when.

- **The negative control needs `USERPROFILE` faked, not just `HOME`.** `spike/tail.mjs:28` resolves via
  `os.homedir()`, which reads `USERPROFILE` on Windows. Faking only `HOME` runs happily against the
  **real** `~/.claude` and reports `RESOLVED 36` — a green, confident, completely false pass on the one
  check whose entire purpose is proving we never touch it. Measured, not theorised.

- **`fixtures/hook-events/` is content-free, not anonymous.** Its redaction destroys values but
  deliberately keeps `cwd`, `transcript_path`, `session_id`, `agent_id` and `prompt_id` verbatim,
  because a fixture without them cannot pin the main-thread rule. Paths are backslash-separated
  (`C:\Users\dev\…`) — a privacy sweep greping a forward-slash form finds nothing. Phase 5 must
  cover this directory explicitly.

- **The spike audit fails loudly on a wrong `--project` path — it exits 2, not 0.** An earlier claim
  that it "exits 0 as a silent pass" was false and propagated through an entire phase because it had
  been written into the `phase-verifier`'s memory store by the orchestrator. **Nothing in
  `.claude/agent-memory/` is ground truth** — it is a claim to re-measure, and the party being judged
  must not write there.

- **`"type": "module"` + a CommonJS bundle named `.js` = an extension that silently does not
  activate.** Node resolves a `.js` file's format from the nearest `package.json`, so VS Code parses
  the CJS host bundle as ESM and `module.exports` never reaches it. It does **not throw** — you get
  `activate = undefined` and an inert extension that still builds and still packages. Measured against
  the unzipped VSIX both ways. The host bundle is therefore `dist/extension.cjs`, and
  `src/extension.test.ts` loads whatever path `main` actually names and asserts `activate` is a
  function. **The defect class is "the manifest and the build disagree" and it will recur** — that
  test is the guard, not the naming convention.

- **The truncation marker under-reports at the shipped default.** **Every** payload over 8,192 bytes
  is cut twice — inline ones included, so do not go looking only at the offload path: of the 8
  affected payloads in the capture, **7 never touch `tool-results/`**. `redact` cuts at 8192 and
  appends a correct marker (making the string 8,248 bytes), then the grafter's `preview()` re-cuts
  *that* and re-marks against the length it received. At `previewBytes=8192` all 8 claim
  "8192 of 8248" when the originals run to 63,774 — the marker under-reports the largest by 7.73×.
  `redact.ts` tells callers to budget for the marker; `preview()` does not. Also means
  `agentDeck.previewBytes` above 8192 cannot increase kept bytes. **Phase 4 item, recorded in
  `PLAN.md` with the measurements — do not re-derive it from scratch.**

- **Never write a raw control character into source.** A worker wrote a NUL-injection guard with a
  literal `0x00` byte instead of a backslash-zero escape. The file became **binary to git** — no reviewable diff ever
  again — and it compounds the documented `grep -a` hazard that already costs this repo a trap. Fixing
  the encoding also revealed the guard had never been tested at all. Escapes, always.

- **A module-boundary partition produces silent seams, not crashes.** Phase 3's host emitted
  `<div id="app">` while the webview looked for `#agent-deck-root` and fell back to `document.body`.
  Both packages were internally consistent, both fully tested, and they disagreed — the panel rendered
  into the wrong element and nothing failed. Two agreeing literals is not a contract;
  `src/bridge/contract.ts` holds the single definition. **When you split work by file ownership,
  the bugs land between the files, so mutate the hand-off line rather than the implementation.**

- **A shebang in a `.mjs` file breaks vitest collection — but only in a CRLF checkout.** vite strips
  it with `hashbangRE = /^#!.*\n/`, and JavaScript's `.` does not match `\r`, so the pattern matches
  the LF form and not the CRLF one. `.gitattributes` `text=auto` plus `core.autocrlf=true` means the
  author's working tree holds LF and a fresh checkout holds CRLF: the file imports fine for whoever
  wrote it and throws `SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token` for everyone else. Measured on
  `scripts/privacy-sweep.mjs`; removing the shebang is the fix (nothing here is exec'd directly).
  **This is the fixtures lesson applying to SOURCE** — "verify by cloning and comparing bytes, never
